newsitem.title: VIETNAM: China's parliamentary chief meets Vietnam leaders.
newsitem.headline: China's parliamentary chief meets Vietnam leaders.

text.p: Chinese Politburo member Qiao Shi met Vietnam's prime minister and its National Assembly chairman in Hanoi on Monday in the second top-level visit between the two communist countries since June.

Details of the agenda for Qiao's five-day visit were not given and journalists were only allowed to see him greeting National Assembly Chairman Nong Duc Manh and Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet before being ushered away.
Qiao, chairman of China's National People's Congress and a member of the Politburo's Standing Committee, was also due to meet former Vietnamese prime minister Pham Van Dong.

A meeting with President Le Duc Anh which had been scheduled for Tuesday was cancelled. The Foreign Ministry, responding to reports that Anh had suffered a stroke, said the president was "tired" and needed a rest.

Diplomats and other analysts said Qiao's visit was significant as it came soon after that of Premier Li Peng, who in late June became the highest foreign official to attend a Vietnamese Communist Party Congress.
But they also point out that despite party-to-party ties the two countries have a long history of troubled relations.
In 1979 China sent its military pouring over the border into Vietnam to punish Hanoi for its invasion of Cambodia a few weeks earlier.
China was repulsed, but border differences from that period are still unresolved, as are territorial differences over island-chains in the South China Sea.
